1. Order

BUY MWA on the New York Stock Exchange, £125, DAY limit @ $23.90. Currency USD. The order is pending the next £250 contribution because current pot cash is £0.

Expected first-year costs, assuming a GBP-funded Trading 212 Stocks ISA: £0 commission, £0 custody, £0 UK stamp duty on this US share, no ADR fee, and about £0.19 one-way FX cost at 0.15%. HMRC says foreign shares bought outside the UK do not normally attract Stamp Duty or SDRT (official tax guidance). Total expected cost is about £0.19, or 0.15% of the ticket, below the 2% ceiling; the limit controls the bid-offer price. Trading 212 states that Invest/ISA commission and custody are free and its FX fee is 0.15% (official fee schedule, official FX method).

2. Thesis

Mueller sells mission-critical valves, hydrants, metering and leak-detection equipment into North American water networks, where the installed base, qualification burden and cost of failure support replacement demand and help margins resist competition. Why now: four locally filed years show revenue rising every year, GAAP operating margin widening from 10.1% to 18.8% and FY2025 ROIC reaching 13.1%, while Q3 FY2026 still delivered 4.1% sales growth and a 20.4% GAAP operating margin (earnings.json, prices.json, Q3 release). The market appears to treat the gain as temporary pricing and tariff help; what it may be missing is that foundry investment, portfolio work and the faster-growing Water Management business have reset normalized economics upward while the replacement need remains.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At the FY2026 result currently estimated for 5 November 2026, trigger a full re-read if net sales are below management's $1.470bn lower bound, adjusted EBITDA is below $367m, or free cash flow is no more than 70% of adjusted net income. Any miss is the earliest hard evidence that pricing and execution are not carrying into the full year; it is a warning, not an automatic sale (Q3 outlook, local result date).

Break: At the Q2 FY2027 filing, to be checked no later than 7 May 2027, put the position under §5.1 if trailing-twelve-month GAAP operating margin is below 17.0% while trailing-twelve-month revenue growth is below 3.0%. That combination would show that tariff refunds, compensation timing and pricing produced a peak rather than a durable reset in a growing business; it directly tests the strongest case against (current filing and baseline).

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price, the day after the locally estimated FY2026 result.

Local check: agree. The local annual series is used for filed history, and the company filing is used for the newer Q3 evidence. Local trailing EPS is current through June 2026, has no epsStale or oneOff warning, and price, EPS, valuation and all three capital measures are quoted only from the repo.

6. The case against

The margin expansion may be a peak, not a reset. Q3 gross profit explicitly benefited from higher pricing and tariff refunds while volumes were slightly lower; SG&A benefited from lower incentive compensation, Water Flow Solutions sales fell 0.6%, and inventory absorbed $59.9m of cash in the first nine months. If those aids reverse while inflation, foundry spending and municipal or residential demand soften, a low-looking P/E is capitalising temporarily elevated earnings and both earnings and the multiple can contract together (Q3 release, Q3 filing).

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake again: the order is not a water-infrastructure rebound story. It rests on four filed years of revenue and GAAP margin, explicit capital-return and cash evidence, uses valuation only as a gate, and makes temporary margin support the subject of both falsifier tiers.

1. Order

2. Thesis

Intuit owns tax, accounting, payroll, payments and credit workflows used by roughly 100 million customers, and the embedded records, integrations and expert network give its high margin a better chance of persisting than an AI interface without the underlying financial context (company profile). Why now: FY2026 revenue grew 14%, GAAP operating income grew 20%, QuickBooks Online Accounting grew 23% and TurboTax Live grew 37%, while the share clears Leo's valuation filter on both the local and company-reported GAAP earnings (FY2026 results, prices.json). The market appears to read slower FY2027 guidance as maturity; what it may be missing is that automating more of a customer's financial work can increase paid attach and operating leverage even when the underlying tax-software unit count is flat or down.

The source hierarchy keeps the local figure for the repo-held trailing multiple and the company figure for its fiscal year; both imply a P/E below the local 23.793× fifth-percentile threshold. The oneOff annotation is also answered rather than ignored: the local recurring series ends in April 2026, so it is stale by one quarter, but its more conservative 21.09× P/E still remains in the cheapest decile. Intuit may be harvesting its installed base rather than widening its moat. Total U.S. TurboTax units fell 2%, Q4 QuickBooks growth came from higher prices and mix as well as customer growth, FY2027 guidance slows total revenue to 9%–10%, and Mailchimp is guided down 1% to flat; a general AI agent or government tax-filing option could weaken the front-end relationship before revenue shows it because price and expert attach can temporarily offset lost users. At a 27.4% GAAP operating margin, customer acquisition, AI investment or price resistance has room to make both earnings quality and the multiple contract (FY2026 results and FY2027 guidance).

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake again: this is not a generic AI rebound thesis. The case starts with five years of rising GAAP margins, current revenue and EPS, explicit return-on-capital work and the actual product growth mix; valuation is only the gate, and both falsifier tiers test whether the underlying customer franchises weaken while price and attach make headline revenue look healthier.

1. Order

BUY INTU on Nasdaq, £125, DAY limit @ $345.00. Currency USD. The order is pending the next £250 contribution because current pot cash is £0.

Expected first-year costs, assuming a GBP-funded Trading 212 Stocks ISA: £0 commission, £0 custody, £0 UK stamp duty on this US share, no ADR fee, and about £0.19 one-way FX cost at 0.15%. Total expected cost is about £0.19, or 0.15% of the ticket, below the 2% ceiling; the limit controls the bid-offer price. Trading 212 states that Invest/ISA commission and custody are free and its FX fee is 0.15% (official fee schedule, official FX method).

2. Thesis

Intuit owns tax, accounting, payroll, payments and credit workflows used by roughly 100 million customers, and the embedded records, integrations and expert network give its high margin a better chance of persisting than an AI interface without the underlying financial context (company profile). Why now: FY2026 revenue grew 14%, GAAP operating income grew 20%, QuickBooks Online Accounting grew 23% and TurboTax Live grew 37%, while the share still clears Leo's valuation filter on current GAAP and recurring earnings (FY2026 results, prices.json). The market appears to read slower FY2027 guidance as maturity; what it may be missing is that automating more of a customer's financial work can increase paid attach and operating leverage even when the underlying tax-software unit count is flat or down.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At the Q1 FY2027 result locally estimated for 19 November 2026, trigger a full re-read if total revenue is below management's $4.294bn floor, GAAP operating income is below $716m, or QuickBooks Online Accounting revenue growth falls below 15% while management no longer identifies customer growth as a contributor. The first two are misses against explicit guidance; the third is the earliest disclosed sign that price and mix are masking a weakening user base rather than AI deepening the workflow (FY2027 guidance, local result date).

Break: At the FY2027 results, to be checked by 31 August 2027, put the position under §5.1 if total U.S. TurboTax units decline by 5% or more for the year and QuickBooks Online Accounting revenue growth is below 10%. Weakening volume in both the consumer-tax and small-business franchises would directly show that the installed workflow is being harvested or bypassed rather than strengthened; the FY2026 reference points are a 2% TurboTax unit decline and 23% QuickBooks Online Accounting growth (FY2026 results).

4. Review date

20 November 2026, regardless of price, the day after the locally estimated Q1 FY2027 result.

The published FY2026 statements provide revenue of $21.448bn, cost of revenue of $4.253bn, operating income of $5.884bn, pretax income of $6.017bn, tax of $1.451bn, assets of $36.786bn and current liabilities of $10.163bn.

Local check: agree on current EPS and decision. The local quote is current through July 2026 and now carries the company's official $16.46 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS. The oneOff annotation is also answered rather than ignored: recurring P/E is 21.09× and remains in the cheapest decile. One historical disagreement is retained: earnings.json has FY2025 operating income of $4.938bn and a 26.22% margin, while Intuit's FY2026 comparative table has $4.923bn and 26.14%; the historical row keeps the repo figure under the source hierarchy, and neither number affects the FY2026 thesis.

6. The case against

Intuit may be harvesting its installed base rather than widening its moat. Total U.S. TurboTax units fell 2%, Q4 QuickBooks growth came from higher prices and mix as well as customer growth, FY2027 guidance slows total revenue to 9%–10%, and Mailchimp is guided down 1% to flat; a general AI agent or government tax-filing option could weaken the front-end relationship before revenue shows it because price and expert attach can temporarily offset lost users. At a 27.4% GAAP operating margin, customer acquisition, AI investment or price resistance has room to make both earnings quality and the multiple contract (FY2026 results and FY2027 guidance).

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake again: this is not a generic AI rebound thesis. The case starts with five years of rising GAAP margins, current revenue and EPS, explicit return-on-capital work and the actual product growth mix; valuation is only the gate, and both falsifier tiers test whether the underlying customer franchises weaken while price and attach make headline revenue look healthier.

Do not buy this if you want a predictable compounder. Its limit is that “never interrupt compounding” cannot override the pot's 50% position cap or excuse a broken thesis; the essay itself concedes that stock selection still matters and that losers can go to zero.

3. Candidates

RSGN.SW — SIX Swiss Exchange — R&S Group

Why: The transformer maker's H1 backlog reached a record CHF357.9m, up 17%, with a 19.0% EBITDA margin and 6.4% free-cash-flow margin, while the share is down 46.41% over one year and trades at about 13.2 times trailing earnings (company update, price and valuation).

What would have to be true: The adjusted 10% fall in H1 order intake must be temporary normalisation rather than the start of a transformer down-cycle, and backlog must convert while capacity investment preserves cash generation; otherwise the apparently low multiple is peak-cycle earnings in disguise (detailed update).

AMRC — NYSE — Ameresco

Why: The market value is down about 10% over one year while total project backlog rose 32% to $6.73bn; Q2 added $1.8bn of awards, including $1.2bn of data-centre power work, making this a less-loved route into the power bottleneck rather than another semiconductor (company results, market-value history).

What would have to be true: Awards not yet signed must become contracted revenue, Q2's negative $107.2m operating cash flow must reverse, and 3.2x corporate leverage must stay safely below the 3.5x covenant; the 41.8 times trailing P/E means backlog alone does not make it cheap (company cash-flow detail, Yahoo valuation).

BME.L — London Stock Exchange — B&M European Value Retail

Why: Weak real spending favours value retail, but B&M is not being credited with an easy win: the share is roughly flat over one year, while Q1 France revenue grew 14.6% and like-for-like sales 5.3%; the UK business's 2.3% like-for-like decline keeps expectations grounded (Q1 statement, price history).

What would have to be true: UK weakness must mainly reflect the garden-season comparison rather than lost customer relevance, and the FMCG price investment and range reset must restore sales without permanently sacrificing margin. This is the closest candidate to the 7532.T mistake: the turnaround story is not evidence, so first-hand store observation and filed cash conversion matter more than management's recovery language (FY26 results, strategy §2.2).

LRE.L — London Stock Exchange — Lancashire Holdings

Why: H1 profit after tax rose to $141.7m from $109.2m and the discounted combined ratio improved to 80.7% from 87.4%, while the share is approximately flat over one year and trades near 6.3 times trailing earnings (company results, price, valuation).

What would have to be true: The low multiple must not be capitalising peak insurance pricing; gross premiums already fell from $1.36bn to $1.32bn, so underwriting discipline must preserve the combined ratio as rates soften, and catastrophe, marine and energy losses must stay within the risk budget rather than make the current earnings base unrepeatable (company results).

4. What I wanted and did not have

  • US payrolls, real earnings and real consumer spending: fetched from BLS and BEA. I would want the latest monthly releases available to every weekly Sweep; they changed the consumer read.
  • AI/power-infrastructure order intake and backlog: fetched from NVIDIA, R&S Group, Powell and Ameresco releases. I would want these on company results dates, not every week; backlog quality is company-specific and cannot be replaced by one macro series.
  • A consistent specialty-insurance pricing-cycle series: not held locally, so I worked around it with Lancashire and Beazley company disclosures. Quarterly is sufficient; without it, a low P/E can be peak-cycle earnings masquerading as value.
  • Off-universe prices and valuation: fetched from FT Markets, Yahoo Finance and StockAnalysis. I do not want a second permanent feed: adding the four candidates to watchlist.json lets the existing pipeline fetch and fact-check them independently.

The gaps above were appended to pot/data-wishlist.md.

5. Sources consulted

Local: strategy.md, pot/reading.md, the unlisted saved convexity article, holdings.json, watchlist.json, prices.json, history.json, signals.json, pot/positions.json, and the 28 August Sweep.

External primary sources: US Bureau of Labor Statistics employment and real-earnings releases; US Bureau of Economic Analysis July income/outlays release; IMF July World Economic Outlook briefing; NVIDIA, Powell Industries, R&S Group, Ameresco, B&M, Lancashire and Beazley investor/filing releases. Secondary price and valuation checks: FT Markets/Investors' Chronicle, Yahoo Finance and StockAnalysis. No commentary source was treated as a company fact where a primary release was available.

7532.T check

None of these is an order. RSGN.SW and AMRC could be classic infrastructure-cycle traps if orders do not become cash; BME.L is explicitly a turnaround whose story must be checked in stores and accounts; LRE.L's low P/E may simply reflect earnings near the top of the insurance cycle. All four now enter the ordinary watchlist pipeline so their quotes, earnings and P/E bands can be fetched independently before Leo decides whether any deserves a Deep dive.

Sweep — 29 August 2026

1. Where the world is

What is true

The world is absorbing a genuine increase in electricity use, not just an AI-market narrative. The IEA expects global electricity demand to grow 3.6% in 2026 and 3.8% in 2027, versus 3.0% in 2025; it also expects renewables to overtake coal generation in 2026 and says grid expansion and modernisation are critical to integrating that supply (IEA mid-year update). The local data agree that the physical inputs have moved: copper is up 46.95% over one year, while WTI is up 30.35% over one year but down 9.46% over three months (local macro data).

That investment boom sits beside a less comfortable macro picture. The IMF forecasts 3.0% global growth in 2026 and says disinflation has stalled, with technology momentum offsetting the drag from war (IMF July update). Markets show the same split: Nasdaq is up 23.06% over one year and the S&P 500 19.37%, while the Hang Seng is down 0.13%; US five- and ten-year yields are up 21.14% and 11.66% respectively over one year (local macro data).

What I take from it

Power demand is real, but the first-order trade is crowded enough that a good backlog is no longer sufficient. GE Vernova, Caterpillar and Hammond Power Solutions all reported exceptional demand, but their obviousness is the reason not to promote them here (GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Hammond Power Solutions). The useful candidates are businesses where reported orders or cash generation improved while the price lagged, and where the next check can distinguish conversion from backlog theatre. That produces AMSC and OSIS below.

The stalled-disinflation backdrop also argues for not making this a fourth consecutive list of AI infrastructure names. Novo Nordisk is the counterweight: a familiar, profitable consumer-health franchise where the market is pricing a material deterioration in realised price and competitive position. NVIDIA appears only as a re-look because the newly revised local valuation scan fired on it after results; it is not being rediscovered by the Sweep.

2. Leo's reading

pot/reading.md still has no entry under Entries, but the saved-text folder contains the unlisted 2026-04-14-Convexity-Ivan-Li.md. I read the full saved text despite its absence from the list. It is a method essay, not a stock thesis: allow the right tail to compound, do not mechanically rebalance winners away, and do not confuse a price fall with a broken business.

Since 14 April, its named examples have dispersed: NVDA +10.71%, VOO +10.79%, META −12.75%, NFLX −23.11%, AMZN +6.99% and TSLA −4.24% through 28 August (local price history). That four-month spread neither proves nor disproves a long-horizon convexity argument; NVDA has merely matched VOO over the period.

The argument still fits the written rules. Strategy §5.1 permits a sale only when a falsifier trips, the thesis plays out, or a hard position limit is breached; a mechanical stop-loss and routine rebalancing are absent (strategy). The essay cannot override the 50% pot-position cap, and its claim that losers can be left alone still depends on business-level falsifiers being reviewed. It should produce no watchlist ticker.

3. Candidates

AMSC — Nasdaq — American Superconductor

Why: Revenue rose 30% to a record $94.1m, orders exceeded $130m, twelve-month backlog exceeded $300m and operating cash flow nearly quadrupled to $16m, yet the share price was down 43.40% over one year by 26 August (company results, price source). This is a quieter grid, mining-power and resiliency route than the large turbine and transformer winners.

What would have to be true: Acquired and organic revenue must turn into durable per-share earnings: first-quarter non-GAAP net income fell to $7.6m from $11.6m even as revenue grew, and the company warns that backlog may not convert and that suppliers and government funding matter (company results).

OSIS — Nasdaq — OSI Systems

Why: Fiscal-2026 revenue rose 4% to $1.786bn, non-GAAP EPS rose 11% to $10.35, operating cash flow reached a record $276m and backlog a record $1.9bn, while the shares were down 10.18% over one year at 28 August (company results, price source). Security scanning, optoelectronics and healthcare make it a second-order infrastructure/security name rather than a single-theme defence bet.

What would have to be true: Security deliveries delayed by the Middle East conflict must convert rather than roll forward indefinitely, and the fourth-quarter 4% revenue decline must be timing rather than lost demand. Management's fiscal-2027 target of 5.0–8.1% revenue growth and 7.5–11.0% non-GAAP EPS growth must show up in GAAP cash earnings, not only adjusted guidance (company results).

NVO — NYSE ADR / Nasdaq Copenhagen home listing — Novo Nordisk

Why: Q2 adjusted sales rose 7% and adjusted operating profit 11% at constant exchange rates, and guidance was raised, yet the ADR trades at 11.86 times trailing earnings and has returned only 1.78% over five years (company announcement, price and valuation). It is a profitable healthcare franchise outside the portfolio's technology-heavy centre, with pessimism visible in the multiple.

What would have to be true: GLP-1 volume must offset lower realised prices and intensifying competition without sacrificing earnings quality. The raised full-year range still calls for adjusted sales and operating profit to be flat to down 6%, and Q2 adjustments exclude a DKK6.3bn pipeline-asset impairment and 340B provision effects (company announcement, half-year filing).

NVDA — Nasdaq — NVIDIA — re-look (held)

Why: The revised local Scan now puts trailing P/E at 27.50, the lowest observation and 0th percentile across 261 weeks, while Q2 revenue rose 106% to $96.2bn, data-centre revenue rose 117% to $89.0bn and GAAP gross margin was 75.0% (local signal scan, company results).

What would have to be true: The earnings denominator must be durable: a five-year-low P/E is not the same as a cheap business if hyperscaler capital spending or 75% gross margins normalise. The market still values NVIDIA at $5.51tn and 18.36 times trailing sales, so the P/E signal needs a fresh cash-flow and customer-concentration check before it means value (market data).

4. What I wanted and did not have

  • Global electricity-demand, grid-investment and connection-queue data: fetched from the IEA. I would carry each new or mid-year report into the weekly Sweep, not poll it weekly; it separated genuine physical demand from company promotion.
  • Off-universe price and valuation history: fetched from Yahoo Finance, MarketBeat and Fox Business. This gap was already recorded in the wishlist earlier today; adding AMSC, OSIS and NVO to watchlist.json lets the existing pipeline replace the manual figures on its next run.
  • Company order/backlog conversion: fetched from AMSC and OSI releases. I would want it on results dates, not weekly; the local pipeline carries earnings and prices but not order quality.
  • GLP-1 realised pricing, volumes and material pipeline impairments: fetched from Novo Nordisk's announcement and SEC filing. Quarterly is sufficient; trailing P/E alone cannot distinguish a temporarily cheap franchise from declining economics.

The new gaps above were appended to pot/data-wishlist.md; the existing off-universe-price entry was not duplicated.

5. Sources consulted

Local: strategy.md, pot-design.md, pot/reading.md, the unlisted saved convexity article, holdings.json, watchlist.json, prices.json, history.json, signals.json, pot/positions.json, pot/data-wishlist.md, and both prior Sweep files.

External primary sources: IEA Electricity 2026 and its mid-year update; IMF July World Economic Outlook update; NVIDIA, GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Hammond Power Solutions, AMSC, OSI Systems, Amentum, Atkore and Novo Nordisk releases or filings. Secondary price and valuation checks: Yahoo Finance, StockAnalysis, MarketBeat and Fox Business. GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Hammond, Amentum and Atkore were screening work, not candidates; no commentary source was used as a company fact where a primary release was available.

7532.T check

Nothing here is an order. AMSC and OSIS can both be backlog traps; Novo's low multiple can be an accurate warning that competition and pricing have structurally changed; NVIDIA's low five-year P/E can reflect peak earnings rather than value. The three new names enter the normal pipeline for independent quote, earnings and P/E-band checks, and NVIDIA remains a re-look until Leo chooses a Deep dive.

docs.html:
Run ledger

Generated 2026-09-04 12:07 by npm run pot-report, from the Codex session transcripts under ~/.codex/sessions/ — never from what an agent said about itself.

Cost

Cash cost: £0. Codex is authenticated against a ChatGPT subscription (codex login status → "Logged in using ChatGPT"), so nothing is billed per token. What a run spends is subscription allowance and wall-clock time.

The token columns are kept because that is D12's whole purpose: if this ever moves to metered API credits these are the numbers that would be charged, and runs either side of the switch stay comparable. Fresh is input not served from cache — the part a metered call charges full rate for.
